exercises.title: Read a plan from the inside out
exercises.problemHtml:
Order the nodes of this plan in the order rows start flowing (the innermost, most indented node produces rows first):

Limit
  ->  Sort
        Sort Key: (sum(e.amount)) DESC
        ->  HashAggregate
              Group Key: u.country
              ->  Hash Join
                    Hash Cond: (e.user_id = u.id)
                    ->  Seq Scan on event e
                    ->  Hash
                          ->  Seq Scan on users u

This set has 1 question. There is nothing to run: answer in the panel on the right and press Submit. Work each one out yourself first (on paper or in psql on your own PostgreSQL), then check — every explanation after Submit says why the tempting wrong answer is wrong.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanation of every question appears after you submit.

Limit
  ->  Sort

        ->  HashAggregate
              Group Key: u.country
              ->  Hash Join

                    ->  Seq Scan on event e
                    ->  Hash
                          ->  Seq Scan on users u

exercises.title: EXPLAIN ANALYZE: how many rows did the filter throw away?
exercises.problemHtml:
Run SELECT * FROM event WHERE status = 'pending' under EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, COSTS OFF, TIMING OFF, SUMMARY OFF, BUFFERS OFF) — the options remove every number that changes between runs, so the output is exactly comparable. Your script's last statement is that EXPLAIN.

Sample tables (chapters 9–10)

event (id identity PK, user_id int, status text, amount numeric(10,2), email text, created_at timestamptz, props jsonb)
      20 000 rows: user_id 1–2000 (10 events each) · status pending 1 %, done ~33 %, active ~66 %
      email 'user<g>@example.com' (unique) · created_at every 10 minutes from 2024-01-01 · props {"plan": "free"|"pro", "device": …}
users (id PK, name, country)   2 000 rows
No index except the primary keys. Statistics are collected (ANALYZE) so the planner behaves like on a real server.
Helpers: plan_nodes(q) / plan_text(q) / plan_rows(q) / plan_analyze(q) print the plan of query text q.

The lesson used 500 000 rows; 20 000 deterministic rows are enough for the planner to make the same choices. The grader is PostgreSQL 18 (WASM).

Requirements

  • All five options, in any order.
  • Read the line Rows Removed by Filter — that is wasted work.

users (id PK, name, country)   2 000 rows
No index except the primary keys. Statistics are collected (ANALYZE) so the planner behaves like on a real server.
Helpers: plan_nodes(q) / plan_text(q) / plan_rows(q) / plan_analyze(q) print the plan of query text q.

Bài giảng dùng 500 000 dòng; 20 000 dòng tất định đủ để bộ lập kế hoạch chọn giống vậy. Máy chấm là PostgreSQL 18 (WASM).

Yêu cầu

  • Đủ năm tuỳ chọn, thứ tự tuỳ ý.
  • Đọc dòng Rows Removed by Filter — đó là công sức bỏ phí.

exercises.title: Remove the wasted work you just measured
exercises.problemHtml:
Make SELECT * FROM event WHERE status = 'pending' stop discarding rows: after your change, EXPLAIN ANALYZE of that query must contain no Rows Removed by Filter and still return the 200 pending events. Choose the smallest index that does it.

Sample tables (chapters 9–10)

event (id identity PK, user_id int, status text, amount numeric(10,2), email text, created_at timestamptz, props jsonb)
      20 000 rows: user_id 1–2000 (10 events each) · status pending 1 %, done ~33 %, active ~66 %
      email 'user<g>@example.com' (unique) · created_at every 10 minutes from 2024-01-01 · props {"plan": "free"|"pro", "device": …}
users (id PK, name, country)   2 000 rows
No index except the primary keys. Statistics are collected (ANALYZE) so the planner behaves like on a real server.
Helpers: plan_nodes(q) / plan_text(q) / plan_rows(q) / plan_analyze(q) print the plan of query text q.

The lesson used 500 000 rows; 20 000 deterministic rows are enough for the planner to make the same choices. The grader is PostgreSQL 18 (WASM).

Requirements

  • One CREATE INDEX (a partial one is the smallest).
  • Do not change the query.

solutionCodeJson.name: answers.md
solutionCodeJson.code:
# Estimate, actual, loops: what the numbers mean — answer key

1. Index Scan using users_pkey on users u (actual rows=1.00 loops=200) — how many rows did this node return in total?Index Scan using users_pkey on users u (actual rows=1.00 loops=200) — nút này trả tổng cộng bao nhiêu dòng?
   Answer: b) 200 — 1 row per loop × 200 loops
   Inside a Nested Loop the inner node runs once per outer row; "actual rows" is per execution.VI: Trong Nested Loop, nút bên trong chạy một lần cho mỗi dòng ngoài; "actual rows" tính cho mỗi lần chạy.

2. Seq Scan on event (rows=200) (actual rows=200.00 loops=1) — is the estimate good?Seq Scan on event (rows=200) (actual rows=200.00 loops=1) — ước lượng có tốt không?
   Answer: b) yes — estimate and actual match, the statistics are fine
   Good estimates are the first thing to check. A Seq Scan can still be the right plan.VI: Ước lượng tốt là thứ cần kiểm đầu tiên. Seq Scan vẫn có thể là kế hoạch đúng.

3. Sort Method: external merge Disk: 928kB means…Sort Method: external merge Disk: 928kB nghĩa là…
   Answer: c) the sort did not fit in work_mem and spilled to temporary files
   External merge = sort in chunks on disk. Raising work_mem (for that session or query) or sorting fewer rows fixes it — lesson 10.4.VI: External merge = sắp theo từng khúc trên đĩa. Tăng work_mem (cho phiên hay truy vấn đó) hoặc sắp ít dòng hơn là sửa được — bài 10.4.

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml:

  1. b) 200 — 1 row per loop × 200 loops

    Inside a Nested Loop the inner node runs once per outer row; "actual rows" is per execution.

    VI: Trong Nested Loop, nút bên trong chạy một lần cho mỗi dòng ngoài; "actual rows" tính cho mỗi lần chạy.

  2. b) yes — estimate and actual match, the statistics are fine

    Good estimates are the first thing to check. A Seq Scan can still be the right plan.

    VI: Ước lượng tốt là thứ cần kiểm đầu tiên. Seq Scan vẫn có thể là kế hoạch đúng.

    External merge = sort in chunks on disk. Raising work_mem (for that session or query) or sorting fewer rows fixes it — lesson 10.4.
